title: BalancerPoolerV2.migrateMint is reachable while every pause / disable surface in the system is engaged — documented as intentional but operator runbook gap
severity_rationale:
Low (DOWNGRADED from econ-scanner's tentative Medium). The project's own test `test_migrateMint_runsWhenPaused` (test/V2/BalancerPoolerV2.t.sol:1732) explicitly asserts that migrateMint executes after `pooler.pause()`. The pause-bypass behaviour is the INTENDED design — migrations are meant to be a one-shot exit path that does NOT depend on the operator keeping the protocol unpaused. This is a documentation / runbook gap rather than a security gap.

Three independent pause surfaces (NFTMinterV2.paused, BalancerPoolerV2.paused, configs[6].disabled) are bypassed, but the residual risk during an incident is bounded: migrateMint is 1:1 (one id-4 burns to mint one id-6), so it cannot inflate supply beyond the existing id-4 cohort. The operator has owner-only revocation levers (setAuthorizedBurner(pooler, false), setAuthorizedMinter(pooler, false)) that DO halt migration; the gap is that they are slower than the pauser. Per C4 Medium requires 'function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted, or leak value with stated assumptions' — the migration's pause-bypass does not impact the protocol's broader availability and does not leak value beyond the id-4->id-6 conversion the user is entitled to perform. QA/Low classification applies: spec-vs-runbook deviation without value leak.

Note: the new `ECON-RAW-010` from this run (reentrancy) is unrelated to the report-6 known-issue file of the same name. Pause-bypass is captured here.
description:
migrateMint has no whenNotPaused gate. It calls into NFTMinterV2.burn (gated only by authorizedBurners, no paused check) and NFTMinterV2.mintFor (gated only by authorizedMinters, no paused / disabled check). Three independent pause levers exist in the system:
  (1) NFTMinterV2.paused (global, set via Pauser)
  (2) BalancerPoolerV2.paused (per-dispatcher, set via setDispatcherActive(false))
  (3) configs[6].disabled (per-id, set via setDispatcherDisabled(6, true))
migrateMint honours NONE of them. By contrast, the paid path `_executeMint` checks BOTH (1) and (3).

The project's own test `test_migrateMint_runsWhenPaused` at test/V2/BalancerPoolerV2.t.sol:1732 explicitly asserts that migrateMint succeeds after `pooler.pause()`. This makes the behaviour an INTENTIONAL design choice — migrations are positioned as a one-shot exit path that should keep working even when the rest of the protocol is paused. Reasonable framing for a migration; the issue is operational legibility.

During an incident the operator-mental-model is 'engage every pause switch and investigate.' If the incident is related to the id-4 cohort itself (e.g., a flaw in the original BalancerPoolerV2 lifecycle that makes id-4 supply contested, or a flaw discovered in the new pooler post-replaceDispatcher), the operator needs additional owner-only txs — setAuthorizedBurner(pooler, false), setAuthorizedMinter(pooler, false) — to halt migration. Both require the owner key, which is the slowest control plane in the system. There is no documented runbook line item that calls these out alongside the standard pauses.

Merged from: RAW-005 (pause-topology gap framing) and ECON-RAW-008 (three-pause-surfaces-bypassed framing).
exploit_path:
1. Incident detected. Pauser calls `NFTMinterV2.pause()` (sets global paused = true) and `setDispatcherActive(pooler, false)` (sets dispatcher paused = true). Operator believes mint and migration surfaces are frozen.
2. Any id-4 holder calls `BalancerPoolerV2.migrateMint(amount, recipient)`. Call traverses migrateMint -> burn -> mintFor -> ERC1155._mint. None of the four call sites consult either pause flag. Migration proceeds and continues to fire ClaimBurned and ClaimMintedFor events as if no incident.
3. To stop migration, the operator must additionally send `NFTMinterV2.setAuthorizedBurner(pooler, false)` and `NFTMinterV2.setAuthorizedMinter(pooler, false)` — owner-only txs that take longer than the pauser path.
4. In the window between pause and revocation, id-4 holders continue to convert into id-6. If the incident is on the id-4 cohort itself, this is operationally damaging.

Note: this is the intended design per the project's test suite. The operational damage above is the cost the team accepted in exchange for migration availability during pause.
mainnet_realism_check: Three independent pause surfaces all silently bypassable on the migrate path. test_migrateMint_runsWhenPaused already confirms the bypass at the dispatcher level; the bypass at NFTMinterV2.mintFor level is the report-6 RAW-002 issue, still present at HEAD. No mock dependency; no AMM dependency.
recommendation:
Two reasonable paths:

(a) Accept the design (migrations bypass pause is intentional) and DOCUMENT it clearly: add NatSpec to migrateMint stating 'this function intentionally bypasses all pause surfaces. To halt migrations the operator must call setAuthorizedBurner(pooler, false) and setAuthorizedMinter(pooler, false). This MUST be part of the incident response runbook.' Add the same lines to the operator runbook / deployment doc.

(b) Add a single dedicated gate: a `migrationOpen` boolean (settable by owner, defaulting true at deploy, settable to false irreversibly) on the pooler. This gives the operator a single fast lever to halt migrations that does not require touching authorizedBurner/authorizedMinter (which may have other dependents). Distinct from the broader pause so migrations can remain available during routine pauses but be halted during a migration-specific incident.

(a) is sufficient and matches the team's existing intent. (b) is a small upgrade that materially improves the operator's incident-response surface.
